lastReply:
People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a text. You open any app, scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves in seconds. No cash to count, no change to hunt for, no card machine needed.

It also works everywhere. The same system runs on many apps, so you can pay a chai seller, a friend or a big shop the same way. Even the smallest vendors can accept money with just a printed QR code.

Here are the 3 main reasons:

It is free for most people. Sending money between bank accounts usually costs nothing, which beats card fees and wallet charges.
It is fast and works anytime. Payments go through in seconds, day or night, including holidays, straight from bank to bank.
It is simple and everywhere. One QR code or phone number is enough, so shops of every size accept it, and a basic smartphone is all you need.

Add to that the push from banks, apps and cashback offers in the early days, and many people simply never went back to cash. Fees, limits and offers can change, so check your bank's current rules.
